topic: cache load protection and coordination pitfalls

method.selection: Official command and library contracts checked against selected vendor advice and previously read primary accounts.
method.scope: Documentation and research only; reference authoring authorized separately. No production actions, downloaded source bodies, code execution experiments or model trials.
method.inference: Practice mechanisms, scope decisions and test schedules are original conditional application guidance, not claims that Redis supplies a cross-store atomic protocol.

sources.title: Optimal Probabilistic Cache Stampede Prevention
sources.version_scope: Andrea Vattani, Flavio Chierichetti, Keegan Lowenstein; PVLDB Vol. 8 No. 8
sources.access: public author-hosted full PDF; selected text read
sources.read_scope: Abstract, expected stampede result around Theorem 7, complete implementation notes section 5 and Figure 3 on PDF page 6; mathematical proofs and full paper not reviewed.

practices.trigger: Many entries share an expiration time.
practices.mechanism: Spread deadlines independently within the allowed freshness ceiling; measure miss distribution.
practices.limits: One hot key still needs a shared loader; jitter is not refresh-ahead.
practices.counterexample: An immutable low-traffic object needs neither periodic refresh nor an elaborate jitter policy.
practices.verification: Use a fixed random seed and fake clock; assert all deadlines remain within the maximum and expiry is spread.
practices.novelty: New concrete cache technique; existing retry jitter concerns a different clock.

practices.trigger: Frequently read data should refresh before its hard serving deadline.
practices.failure: Slow or failed refresh becomes synchronized misses or silently unbounded stale serving.
practices.mechanism: Separate soft refresh time from hard expiry, bound refresh work, coalesce loaders and preserve source age/revision.
practices.limits: The buffer is measured against latency and retry budget; expiry notifications cannot trigger reliably before deletion.
practices.counterexample: Strict current-state authorization may require the authority on every decision.
practices.verification: Delay or fail refresh across both deadlines; assert allowed stale behavior ends at the hard boundary.
practices.novelty: Adds explicit timing and failure contract to existing staleness and admission guidance.

practices.trigger: Early refresh is considered without a shared coordination service.
practices.failure: Expected load reduction is mistaken for exactly one refresher or guaranteed timely renewal.
practices.mechanism: Treat sampling as probabilistic admission, preserve hard freshness limits and bound origin work; coordinate if overlap is unacceptable.
practices.limits: Zero or multiple contenders can occur. A measured refresh duration and workload assumptions affect tuning.
practices.counterexample: A source allowing only one active operation requires stronger coordination than random selection.
practices.verification: Inject random outcomes selecting zero and multiple contenders; assert bounded origin admission and hard-expiry behavior.
practices.novelty: Corrects the new user-provided exactly-one claim with a concise reference paragraph.

practices.trigger: Repeated requests for absent objects hit the source.
practices.failure: A stale negative hides a newly created record, or a shared negative crosses visibility boundaries.
practices.mechanism: Cache authoritative absence with short bounded retention; scope equivalence, enforce authorization, bound distinct keys, and condition publication when creation must become immediately visible.
practices.limits: A timeout is not absence. Short TTL permits a stale window unless a stronger protocol closes it.
practices.counterexample: One-off random IDs may cost more cache space than repeated source lookups; admission still matters.
practices.verification: Pause absent lookup, create object, invalidate, then release old lookup; include tenants with equal IDs and an origin timeout.
practices.novelty: Concrete negative-entry treatment; stale-fill and scope mechanisms already exist elsewhere.

practices.trigger: Mostly absent-key traffic makes authoritative misses expensive.
practices.failure: An unready, lost or lagging filter suppresses an existing database record.
practices.mechanism: Promote a caught-up generation; keep membership synchronized with request-visible writes. Treat positive as a lookup and uncertain readiness as bounded fallback or unavailability.
practices.limits: No data-structure false negatives does not imply database completeness. Readiness and membership need a protocol against replacement/loss. Retained deletions cause extra lookups; rebuild rather than clear shared bits.
practices.counterexample: Mostly existing-key traffic gains little; authoritative uniqueness and authorization still apply.
practices.verification: Commit before membership update; lose filter between readiness and query; rebuild while writes continue; positive for an absent key still performs authoritative lookup.
practices.novelty: Substantive gap; no Bloom filter coverage in audited packages.

practices.trigger: Operational code enumerates a large live Redis keyspace.
practices.failure: Blocking traversal or unbounded follow-up batches disrupt foreground traffic.
practices.mechanism: Pace SCAN until cursor zero, handle duplicates and empty nonterminal batches, and bound processing concurrency.
practices.limits: COUNT is a hint; mutations prevent exact-snapshot claims. Verify shard coverage; a complete traversal still costs linear work.
practices.counterexample: An isolated bounded development database can tolerate KEYS; exact accounting needs another representation.
practices.verification: Inject repeated keys and an empty intermediate batch; mutate keys during traversal and measure foreground latency.

practices.trigger: Concurrent equivalent reads miss one hot key.
practices.failure: Waiter cancellation kills another caller’s load, waiters leak, or failures release a new stampede.
practices.mechanism: Define equivalent identity and loader ownership; bound load duration, waiters, distinct keys and origin concurrency; clean the registry on all exits.
practices.limits: Process-local coordination does not suppress another process. Forget can allow an overlapping load; cancellation is not built into singleflight’s documented API.
practices.counterexample: Different visibility or freshness requirements cannot blindly share a result.
practices.verification: Cancel one waiter while another succeeds; fail the owner; saturate distinct keys; use two coordination groups and expect independent loads.
practices.novelty: Being implemented by research_storage in capacity.md; avoid duplication in the new reference.

practices.trigger: A shared loader or worker uses an expiring distributed lock.
practices.failure: An old holder deletes a successor’s lock or keeps writing after ownership becomes uncertain.
practices.mechanism: Use a unique acquisition token with atomic owner-checked release/renewal; stop starting protected work on uncertain renewal. Enforce stale-owner rejection at the resource when correctness requires it.
practices.limits: A token safe for unlock is not ordered fencing; resource checks do not automatically revoke earlier owners at TTL expiry. Async failover and clocks are protocol assumptions.
practices.counterexample: An efficiency-only read lock can tolerate overlap if duplicate work and late fills remain safe.
practices.verification: Pause past expiry, acquire a successor, release the old token, lose renewal acknowledgement and deliver an old write after a new generation.
practices.novelty: Fencing already thorough. Root authorized one conditional Redis-loader paragraph covering atomic owner-token release/renewal and uncertainty in cache-coherence.md; idempotency unchanged.
